svg.text: FinSight AI, Phase 1: how one company's data is kept separate from another's
Two independent locks in Aurora (a partition per company first, a row-level rule second), plus the company id on every call. The pilot runs one cell; the same rules repeat per region and cell.
Phase 1 scope: ingestion, question answering with citations, and the source viewer. Standard setup shown, with pilot values named where they differ.

1. The Global router picks the region first; identity and tenancy run inside the region
HLD order: company to region and cell lookup happens before any regional component. The edge stack below only exists in the chosen region.
Web app
Next.js: upload form, chat,

Global router
The first global step. Maps company_id
to (region, cell) before anything else.
Other regions
Same setup, added later.
A company is never half moved.
Pre-auth company lookup
Company id comes from the request or a
stored mapping; auth happens in-region.
Edge
CloudFront and WAF.
Rate limits from config.
API Gateway
REST and streaming, TLS.
Rate limits per second/burst.
Cognito (Lite)
4 groups -> 4 roles.
No third-party vendor (D8).
Authorizer -> RequestContext
company_id . user_id . role . access_scope . cell . trace_id
Built once, then read-only for the rest of the request.
config/permissions.yaml is the only source of access
Role x action x document category. documents.categories must match it exactly.
An unknown role, a missing entry or an unknown category stops startup. It never defaults.
A missing permission is denied. There is no default allow on any role.
Role lookup cache lives in DynamoDB, never function memory; privileged roles read live (5.18).
Role changes bump the role version; running copies see it on the next call or within 60 seconds.
Authorizer -> RequestContext, immutable, then tenancy and storage use it
company_id comes from the verified token claim, never from the request body.
The token's company must match the company the router routed. Otherwise: refused.
The Global router's resolved cell is folded in here, so the cell is part of the context.
Pilot: scale.cells = 1, so every company maps to cell 1; a missing or doubled cell stops startup.
Use cases receive this context, so company and cell cannot be widened later.
2. The router picks one cell per company. One database per cell, and no query crosses cells.
Residency note: the router and CloudFront are global, but each company is hosted in one region and its data stays there. Risk 9 is still open.

Aurora + pgvector

DynamoDB

Cell 2 and up
Created only when listed in config.
The pilot creates none, so there
is no extra cost.
Rules the config module enforces
Every company maps to exactly one cell.
scale.vector_store must name a registered store.
Moving a company is copy, verify, switch, then delete.
3. Inside a cell: shared parent tables, then two independent locks around each company
Every query carries company_id. Lock 1 decides which rows can be touched, lock 2 decides which rows may be returned.
Shared parent tables, PARTITION BY LIST (company_id)
documents . document_versions . pages . document_chunks (vectors) . metrics (extracted numbers)
Onboarding adds a partition, its indexes and
its vector index before the first upload.
The upload endpoint refuses with a clear
message while a partition is missing.
Partition for company A
Only rows with company_id = A can land here.
Own HNSW vector index and own company-first indexes.
Own retention: dropped when the company leaves.
A query names the company, so the planner prunes to this one box.
Partition for company B
Only rows with company_id = B can land here.
Own HNSW vector index and own company-first indexes.
Own retention: dropped when the company leaves.
A query names the company, so the planner prunes to this one box.
Partition for company C
Only rows with company_id = C can land here.
Own HNSW vector index and own company-first indexes.
Own retention: dropped when the company leaves.
A query names the company, so the planner prunes to this one box.
LOCK 1, physical: partition pruning
Partitions keep each company's rows in their own place and give each its own vector index, so search stays fast within one company.
Lock 1 is performance and blast radius. A missing filter never happens on purpose, and it does not refuse by itself; that is Lock 2's job.
LOCK 2, logical: row-level security, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every parent table
Policy: USING (company_id = current_setting('app.company_id')::uuid). The value is set from the context inside the UnitOfWork, per transaction.
If a query forgets the filter, Postgres returns zero rows. If the setting is missing, it fails closed, never open. Reset when the connection returns to the pool.
Both locks stay on in every environment. Neither is a switch, and neither has an off path.
4. The same company id reaches every other store, and each store keys on it in its own way
Aurora is the truth for documents and jobs. Everything else is either rebuildable, or addressed by a key that already contains the company.
S3 raw files
Bucket per environment and region, KMS.
One prefix per company, for example
<company_id>/<document_id>/<version>/.
A signed link is short-lived and covers
one file. The source viewer re-checks
access before it signs anything.
Answer cache (DynamoDB)
Key built in one function and unit tested
(see the strip below).
TTL from cache.ttl_seconds. BASE is fine.
Company and role are checked again on read.
Upload, update or deletion bumps the stamp,
so old answers become unaddressable.
Role cache and job view
DynamoDB. Role cache keyed by user id,
plus one role version per company.
Role version read strongly consistent.
Job progress here is rebuildable; Aurora
is the truth. Chat history is company
scoped and never reused for another.
SQS and Step Functions
One queue per cell, with a per-company
cap on running jobs (5.21).
The job carries the company id; the
worker rebuilds RequestContext.
Safe to repeat: job id plus upsert on
chunk id. Retry list after the limit.
The answer cache key, in full
company id
from the token
role
1 of 4 roles
access scope
allowed categories
question
hash of the text
document stamp
moved on every write
Change any one part and the key changes. Upload, update or a deletion moves the stamp in the same transaction, so old answers become unaddressable.
The stamp is one row per company. Entries are not deleted in a race, they simply stop being reachable, and TTL clears the rest.
A cached answer is only shown after the same role and category check a fresh answer would face.
Read paths that must not go stale
fresh_read_window_seconds 10: reads right after an
upload use the primary, not the standby reader (5.9).
A cached answer carries its model name and a
cache tag, so it is never mistaken for a fresh one.
Privileged roles never read a cached role.
5. Where each lock sits in the two flows
The write path proves where rows land. The read path proves which rows can come back, including through a citation.
Write path: upload to a committed version
1. Input gate: category, period, status, upload type, file type and size.
2. Onboarding gate: the company partition must exist, or the upload is refused.
3. S3: the object lands under the company prefix, encrypted.
4. Virus scan: only after the file is in S3. The job is queued only if it passes.
5. SQS to Step Functions: the job carries the company id and the per-company cap.
6. Read, delta check, chunk, embed: the worker rebuilds the context and sets RLS.
7. One transaction: pages, chunks, vectors, extracted numbers, version, job status, stamp.
8. Lock 1 places the rows in one partition. Lock 2 stops any other read returning them.
9. Commit, then ready. Cache entries on the old stamp are no longer addressable.
Read path: question, answer, citation
1. Authorizer to RequestContext. Role checked against permissions.yaml on every call.
2. Input gate runs before any model: prompt trick checks and PII checks.
3. Cache lookup with company, role, scope and stamp. Company checked again on read.
4. Understand, then embed the question. The embedding model version is stored.
5. Hybrid search, company first, inside that company's partition and vector index.
6. Rerank sees only the chunks the company-scoped search returned, never a pool.
7. Calculate with code inside the same tenant context. The model never does maths.
8. Evidence gate, model router and gateway, output gate on citations and numbers.
9. Citation to source viewer: a citation id on its own is never enough (below).
What the source viewer checks before it returns one row
1. The citation resolves to a document inside the context's company.
2. The role may see that document category, per permissions.yaml.
3. The version is visible: not soft-deleted, not superseded without a note.
4. Only then is the page or table read, and a short-lived link signed.
Where a number in an answer comes from
Every figure is produced by SQL or pandas, inside the same tenant context.
The model may repeat a figure from code output or from a cited chunk, nothing else.
The output gate drops any sentence whose number cannot be traced to one of those.
So a neighbour's number cannot enter through a shared prompt part either.
6. Cross-company attempts, and where each one stops
Every row names the lock or check that refuses the request. None of these rely on the caller behaving well.
Attempt
Where it stops
Send another company_id in the request body
Ignored. The context is built from the token claim, and the body cannot set or change the company.
Guess a document or chunk id from another company
The repository filter plus lock 2. Zero rows, and no error tells the caller whether the row exists.
Open a citation id from another company in the viewer
The source viewer compares document.company_id with the context before it reads or signs anything.
Ask a question whose best chunks belong to a neighbour
Search runs inside one partition with the company named first. The neighbour's rows are never candidates.
Replay a pre-signed upload link
Links are short-lived and cover one file. A download is re-authorized before it is signed.
Keep using a role that was just removed
The role version is bumped. Privileged roles read fresh every call, others within 60 seconds.
Put a job for another company on the queue
The worker rebuilds the context from the job record and re-sets RLS. A repeated message does no harm.
Ship a query that forgets the company filter
Lock 2 returns zero rows. A test build also rejects a repository method without company_id.
Expect a stale answer after an upload
The stamp moves in the same transaction, so the old cache key is no longer addressable.
Pull a soft-deleted document
Queries exclude deleted rows, purge waits deleted_retention_days, and the audit entry stays.
7. None of this is a switch, and this is how the build proves it
Every item below is on in every environment and has no off path. A failure in any of these tests blocks a release.
Protections that never turn off
company id on every repository, search, cache, queue and storage call
row-level security on the parent tables, plus the partition-per-company gate
the output gate, which has no off value in config
metering, the audit log and the write-once copy
Shared on purpose: code, model providers, one database per cell.
Never shared: rows, files, vectors, cached answers, usage detail.
Tests that fail the build if separation breaks
RLS test: a query without the setting returns nothing, and does not error open
company filter test: every repository method requires company_id
cache key test: the key changes when company, role, scope or stamp changes
cross-company isolation test across every endpoint, including the source viewer
partition-missing upload test, negative source viewer test
Feedback can enter the golden set after review and anonymising. Nothing learned from one company is used for another.
Grounded in docs/plans/phase1/phase1_mvp_plan.md (D1, D2, D3, D7, D8), finsight_mvp_hld.svg, finsight_config_switches.md 5.15, 5.18, 5.20, 5.21, 5.27 and CODING_STANDARDS.md section 11.
